cards.notes: Bring a class project or an idea to test; this technology hub combines specialized labs and equipment support for coursework.
cards.short_summary: A library technology hub built for hands-on, cross-disciplinary project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins describes Area 49 as a technology hub for collaboration, experimentation, and exploration, with labs and equipment lending for classwork.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Atkins Library; ask the Area 49 Desk about equipment and lab use.

cards.title: EZ Video Studios

cards.evidence_claim: Atkins lists three EZ Video Studios among the specialized spaces in Area 49.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Area 49 at Atkins Library; confirm availability and reservation requirements with the library.

cards.title: Gaming Lab
cards.subtitle: Area 49, Atkins Library
cards.notes: Plan a project session around the lab’s specialized setting, and ask Area 49 staff which equipment and use options are available.
cards.short_summary: A named specialized lab within Atkins Library’s collaborative technology area.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins identifies the Gaming Lab as one of Area 49’s technology spaces for students and researchers.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Area 49 at Atkins Library; follow library and equipment-use guidance.

cards.title: MakerSpace
cards.subtitle: Area 49, Atkins Library
cards.notes: Start with a coursework or prototype idea, then check with Area 49 staff about the available tools and current use procedures.

cards.evidence_claim: Atkins lists the MakerSpace as part of Area 49, which supports student and researcher access to specialized equipment.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Area 49 at Atkins Library; staff assist users with the labs and equipment.

cards.title: Visualization Lab
cards.subtitle: Area 49, Atkins Library
cards.notes: Consider this lab for a technology-based course project, and consult the Area 49 Desk for current equipment and access details.
cards.short_summary: A visualization-focused lab in the library’s technology-intensive second-floor area.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins includes the Visualization Lab among Area 49’s specialized spaces and describes the area as supporting technology use in coursework.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Area 49 at Atkins Library; ask staff about available services before planning work.

cards.title: Teaching + Technology Theater (T3)
cards.subtitle: Area 49, Atkins Library
cards.notes: Use this named technology space as a starting point for supported classwork; verify current room access with the Area 49 Desk.
cards.short_summary: A technology theater within Area 49’s cluster of project-oriented library spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins lists the Teaching + Technology Theater (T3) as a specialized Area 49 space supporting student and researcher technology access.
cards.source_title: Gold Nuggets | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Area 49 at Atkins Library; availability may depend on library procedures.

cards.title: Graduate and Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Atkins Library, Room 115
cards.notes: Choose this room for distraction-free independent work; mute devices and keep the space silent for everyone using it.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study room for graduate students and others seeking quiet.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins identifies Room 115 as Graduate and Silent Study, with the west side designated for graduate students and anyone wanting distraction-free work.
cards.source_title: Study & Quiet/Silent Spaces | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Silent study: no group study or conversations; mute phones and use headphones or earbuds.

cards.title: Atkins Library Nap Pods
cards.subtitle: Atkins Library, third-floor east-side nook
cards.notes: Reserve a one-hour session when you need a quiet reset, then wipe the pod before and after use as library policy requires.
cards.short_summary: Three reservable one-person nap pods overlooking the Student Activities Center and Halton Arena.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins says three Nap Pods are in the third-floor east-side nook and are reservable for one-hour sessions through its study-room system.
cards.source_title: Study & Quiet/Silent Spaces | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: For active UNC Charlotte students, faculty, and staff with valid university ID; reserve through the library system.

cards.title: VanLandingham Glen
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Walk the woodland trails at an unhurried pace, or use the picnic tables and hammock zones while respecting the planted collections.
cards.short_summary: A seven-acre woodland garden with native Carolina plants and hybrid rhododendrons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gardens describe VanLandingham Glen as a 7-acre woodland with over 1,000 native Carolina plant species and an extensive rhododendron collection.
cards.source_title: Collections and Programs | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are open dawn to dusk daily; remain on paths and account for uneven outdoor terrain.

cards.title: McMillan Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Visit during weekday greenhouse hours to see its themed plant rooms, then sign in at the entrance as the Gardens request.
cards.short_summary: A greenhouse with themed collections ranging from orchids and tropical plants to desert succulents.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens says McMillan Greenhouse contains six themed collections across eight greenhouse rooms, terraces, beds, and a courtyard.
cards.source_title: Gardens and Greenhouse | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; admission to the Greenhouse and Gardens is free, with visitor sign-in requested.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-cost ways to spend time on campus, centered on Botanical Gardens access and the free on-campus transit system.

cards.title: Browse the McMillan Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Stop in during weekday greenhouse hours to look through the tropical, desert, orchid, and carnivorous-plant displays without paying admission.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor botanical stop with year-round plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Botanical Gardens and Greenhouse is always free; McMillan Greenhouse is open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Admission & Hours | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Admission is always free; optional donations are welcomed.

cards.title: Walk the Susie Harwood Garden
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk through the outdoor garden’s Carolina Piedmont plantings; use the paths and displays for an easy conversation-paced lap.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor garden with ornamental plants and varied garden styles.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanical Gardens’ admission is always free, and the Susie Harwood Garden is open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden is open daily dawn to dusk. Events and photography sessions may require separate registration and payment.

cards.title: Take the Glen trails
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Follow the wooded garden trails at your own pace, then pause at a bench or picnic table rather than treating the visit as a scheduled program.
cards.short_summary: A free woodland garden with native Carolina plants and rhododendrons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanical Gardens’ admission is always free, and Van Landingham Glen is open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden is open daily dawn to dusk; stay on established trails and plan around daylight.

cards.title: Explore the Native Terrace
cards.subtitle: Inside Susie Harwood Garden, UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Make the terrace a shared plant-spotting stop: follow its meadow and hardscaping, then compare which native blooms or textures catch your attention.
cards.short_summary: A named native-plant collection within the free Botanical Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: Mellichamp Native Terrace is an addition to the Susie Harwood Garden, and admission to the Botanical Gardens is always free.
cards.source_title: Susie Harwood Garden | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Located in the outdoor Susie Harwood Garden, open daily dawn to dusk; general garden admission is free.

cards.title: Meet at the Asian Garden Moon Gate
cards.subtitle: Inside Susie Harwood Garden, UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Use the Moon Gate and decorative-rock collection as a landmark for a slow loop through the garden; keep the visit to regular outdoor garden access.
cards.short_summary: A named garden collection with an iconic Moon Gate.
cards.evidence_claim: The Asian Garden is a collection within the Susie Harwood Garden, and Botanical Gardens admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Susie Harwood Garden | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: In the outdoor gardens, which are open during daylight hours; admission is free.

cards.title: Follow the Winter Trail
cards.subtitle: Susie Harwood Garden, UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Visit in daylight and trace the marked winter-interest plantings through the Harwood Garden; it is a self-guided outdoor option rather than a ticketed tour.
cards.short_summary: A named seasonal trail through the free Harwood Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The Winter Trail is in the Susie Harwood Garden; the outdoor gardens are open to visitors during daylight hours and admission is free.
cards.source_title: Seasonal Highlights | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Available as part of outdoor-garden access during daylight hours; garden admission is free.

cards.title: Check out a garden hammock
cards.subtitle: McMillan Greenhouse and designated hammock zones
cards.notes: Drop into the greenhouse while it is open, borrow a hammock, and use a designated garden hammock zone for a low-key outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A free hammock loan for use in the Botanical Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanical Gardens states that visitors can check out a hammock for free during McMillan Greenhouse open hours.
cards.source_title: Niner Nation | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Drop in while McMillan Greenhouse is open, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; use designated hammock zones.

cards.title: Borrow an art kit in the Gardens
cards.subtitle: McMillan Greenhouse, UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Pick up a free art kit during greenhouse hours, choose an outdoor garden spot, and make a sketching or drawing session out of the visit.
cards.short_summary: A free art-kit loan that turns a garden visit into a creative hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Art kits are available to check out for free whenever the McMillan Greenhouse is open.
cards.source_title: Niner Nation | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Available during McMillan Greenhouse hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Bring a picnic to the Gardens
cards.subtitle: Van Landingham Glen or Susie Harwood Garden
cards.notes: Bring food you already have and meet at the Glen picnic tables or the Harwood Garden’s pond-side picnic area; no garden admission is required.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission outdoor meal break among the gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanical Gardens lists picnic tables in Van Landingham Glen and a large picnic area by the Susie Harwood Garden pond; admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Niner Nation | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Bring your own food. Outdoor gardens are open during daylight hours and general admission is free.

cards.title: Ride the Green Line around campus
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte on-campus transit
cards.notes: Use the on-campus Niner Transit system to link a few campus stops, then get off for a walk or meet-up; no ID or fare is required.
cards.short_summary: Free on-campus bus transportation for any rider.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte states that Niner Transit, its on-campus bus system, is free for everyone and requires no UNC Charlotte ID.
cards.source_title: FAQ | UNC Charlotte Online
cards.access_notes: Free for everyone; no UNC Charlotte ID required. This applies to Niner Transit, not off-campus CATS bus or light-rail service.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UNC Charlotte traditions centered on campus landmarks, Niner identity, and recurring University events.

cards.entity_name: Put a Penny in Norm's Pan
cards.title: Put a Penny in Norm's Pan
cards.subtitle: Norm the Niner statue tradition
cards.notes: Find the 49er Miner statue and place a penny in Norm’s pan as listed by UNC Charlotte’s official traditions site.
cards.short_summary: A small ritual built around the campus’s named miner statue.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Put a Penny in Norm's Pan” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal campus access; follow any posted rules around the statue.

cards.title: Rub the Golden Nugget
cards.subtitle: Campus good-luck ritual
cards.notes: Locate the Golden Nugget and give it a rub while exploring campus; UNC Charlotte identifies this as a Niner tradition.
cards.short_summary: A tactile campus ritual with a distinctly 49er name.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Rub the Golden Nugget” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal campus access and respect the site and surrounding pedestrian areas.

cards.title: Participate in the 49er Ring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Class-ring milestone
cards.notes: If eligible, check University communications for the next 49er Ring Ceremony and follow its registration instructions.
cards.short_summary: A formal milestone tied to the University’s 49er class-ring tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists participation in the 49er Ring Ceremony as a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Eligibility, registration, and any ring-related charges are determined by the current ceremony organizer.

cards.title: Don't Step on the Seal
cards.subtitle: Campus-seal superstition
cards.notes: Watch for the University seal underfoot and take the long way around it, following the tradition named by UNC Charlotte.
cards.short_summary: A lighthearted rule of passage around a recognizable campus emblem.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Don't Step on the Seal” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Use normal pedestrian routes and avoid obstructing others near the seal.

cards.title: Experience the Star Quad Echo
cards.subtitle: Star Quad acoustic tradition
cards.notes: Bring a friend to Star Quad and listen for the echo effect, one of the experiences highlighted by UNC Charlotte.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus sound experiment tied to a named quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Experience the Star Quad Echo” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Try it during normal campus access without disrupting nearby classes, events, or pedestrians.

cards.title: Attend Gold Rush Events
cards.subtitle: Semester welcome-program tradition
cards.notes: Check the current Gold Rush schedule and choose an event that fits your interests during the University’s semester welcome program.
cards.short_summary: A recurring welcome program designed to introduce Niner Pride and campus connections.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte describes Gold Rush as its semester welcome program and says it teaches campus traditions and Niner Pride.
cards.source_title: Year One | Transition & Belonging
cards.access_notes: Event locations, availability, and participation details vary by semester; consult the current University schedule.

cards.title: Wear Green Wednesday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Niner-pride practice
cards.notes: Wear green on Wednesday and use the color as a simple way to take part in the campus tradition.
cards.short_summary: A weekly color ritual that makes Niner identity visible across campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Wear Green Wednesday” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: No special access is required; participation is optional.

cards.title: Stroll through the Botanical Gardens
cards.subtitle: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens tradition
cards.notes: Take a deliberate walk through the Botanical Gardens and use the visit as a quieter stop in the University’s traditions list.
cards.short_summary: A campus nature walk recognized as part of the Niner experience.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Stroll through the Botanical Gardens” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Check current garden and campus access guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Run through the CHHS Rings
cards.subtitle: College of Health and Human Services landmark tradition
cards.notes: Visit the CHHS Rings and pass through the named landmark as part of UNC Charlotte’s official traditions checklist.
cards.short_summary: A movement-based tradition centered on a named campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists “Run through the CHHS Rings” among its campus traditions.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Use the area safely and yield to pedestrians; do not run through it during restricted access or an event setup.

cards.title: Take a Selfie with the Self-Made Man Statue
cards.subtitle: Named campus sculpture tradition
cards.notes: Frame a respectful photo with the Self-Made Man Statue and add this documented stop to a campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A photo tradition anchored by a named piece of campus sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte lists taking a selfie with the Self-Made Man Statue as a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Traditions
cards.access_notes: Visit during normal campus access and avoid blocking walkways or climbing on the sculpture.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Carolina at Charlotte, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that starts with campus welcome programming, then mixes orientation, outdoor time, recreation, and a transit connection.

cards.title: Start with Gold Rush
cards.subtitle: Welcome-program events for new and returning Niners
cards.notes: Check the Gold Rush schedule and choose one free campus event that fits your arrival window; it is designed to introduce resources, traditions, and involvement.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the university’s semester welcome program.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte describes Gold Rush as its semester welcome program; all Gold Rush events are free for students and are hosted by campus departments and student organizations.
cards.source_title: Gold Rush - Niner Engage
cards.access_notes: Check Niner Engage for the current event schedule and any event-specific entry details.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the Union
cards.subtitle: A central campus stop after welcome programming
cards.notes: Use the Popp Martin Student Union as a meeting point, then pause to identify nearby services and campus directions before continuing your first-day walk.
cards.short_summary: Make the student union your first central-campus anchor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte identifies the Popp Martin Student Union as a campus facility and says it was renamed in 2016 to honor alumni Karen Popp and Demond Martin.
cards.source_title: About the Popp Martin Student Union
cards.access_notes: Building access and service availability can vary; check posted Union information when you arrive.

cards.title: Find your library route
cards.subtitle: J. Murrey Atkins Library on the campus core
cards.notes: Walk to the main entrance and save the route from the light-rail shuttle stops; it is a useful reference point for future study sessions and campus navigation.
cards.short_summary: Learn the route to Atkins before classes begin.
cards.evidence_claim: Atkins Library provides directions from the Cone Visitor Parking Deck and identifies Gold Line stop 30 and Green Line stop 44 as Niner Transit stops for reaching the library.
cards.source_title: Directions & Parking | J. Murrey Atkins Library
cards.access_notes: Confirm current library entry and service hours before planning a study visit.

cards.title: Take a daylight garden break
cards.subtitle: Gardens and collections on the east side of campus
cards.notes: Plan a quiet daytime loop through the gardens, sign the visitor log at the greenhouse entrance, and keep the greenhouse’s weekday schedule in mind.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor reset among campus plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte states that admission to the Botanical Gardens and Greenhouse is always free and that the gardens are open daily during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Admission & Hours | UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are open during daylight hours; McMillan Greenhouse is listed as Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Look for seasonal details
cards.subtitle: A named collection within the UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
cards.notes: Add the Susie Harwood Garden to your garden loop and look for its year-round plantings, water features, mosaic patio, and Asian garden elements.
cards.short_summary: A specific garden collection for a slower campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanical Gardens’ FAQ identifies the Susie Harwood Garden and describes year-round interest including camellias, water plants, a mosaic patio, and an Asian garden.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens FAQ
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight hours and follow Botanical Gardens visitor guidance.

cards.title: Walk a piece of the greenway
cards.subtitle: Campus greenway route near recreation spaces
cards.notes: Choose a short daylight walk on Toby Creek Greenway to see how the campus paths connect, then return before dark rather than treating it as a long outing.
cards.short_summary: Use the mapped greenway for an easy orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte’s official web map lists Toby Creek Greenway Trail as a campus map layer.
cards.source_title: UNC Charlotte Web Map
cards.access_notes: Use the official web map and stay on the marked trail during daylight hours.

cards.title: Try a few CORE stations
cards.subtitle: Outdoor fitness equipment beside Toby Creek Greenway
cards.notes: Bring water, choose a few movements that match your experience, and use the open-air CORE equipment as a brief activity stop beside the greenway.
cards.short_summary: A free, all-hours outdoor fitness option by the greenway.
cards.evidence_claim: University Recreation says CORE is adjacent to the on-campus greenway and is open to anyone in the Charlotte community at all hours.
cards.source_title: Our Facilities | University Recreation
cards.access_notes: The official facility page says CORE is open to anyone at all hours; use normal personal-safety judgment and the equipment at your own pace.

cards.title: Scope out UREC
cards.subtitle: University Recreation’s dedicated health and wellness facility
cards.notes: Visit the Recreation Center to locate the pool, courts, equipment desk, and fitness areas, then review membership or student access requirements before participating.
cards.short_summary: Get familiar with the campus recreation hub.
cards.evidence_claim: University Recreation describes UREC as a 148,000-square-foot facility dedicated to health and wellness, with indoor and outdoor pools and recreation spaces.
cards.source_title: Our Facilities | University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Facility participation requires appropriate access; check in with a valid 49er ID or confirm current guest/day-pass rules.

cards.title: Play a casual badminton round
cards.subtitle: Floor 3, Court 4 at UREC
cards.notes: If you have valid UREC access, head to Floor 3, Court 4 for badminton and ask at the equipment desk about what can be checked out.
cards.short_summary: A simple indoor activity with a specifically identified court.
cards.evidence_claim: University Recreation states that badminton is always available at UREC on Floor 3, Court 4, which is divided into three badminton courts.
cards.source_title: Open Recreation | University Recreation
cards.access_notes: Only eligible UNC Charlotte students, UREC members with a valid 49er ID, and eligible alumni may check out equipment; verify access before going.

cards.title: End with a rail orientation
cards.subtitle: LYNX Blue Line terminus at main campus
cards.notes: Walk to the Main Station, open the CATS Pass app if you are a student, and learn the platform location for a future car-free trip into Charlotte.
cards.short_summary: Finish by locating the campus light-rail connection.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Charlotte says the LYNX Blue Line runs from UNC Charlotte to I-485 and that students can board at UNC Charlotte Main Station; students have access to an All-Access Transit Pass.
cards.source_title: Light Rail | Parking and Transportation Services
cards.access_notes: Students should activate their CATS pass before riding; other riders should consult CATS for current fares and schedules.
